body.statement:
The exact law \(\omega^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) and also satisfies \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\).  It has
\[
K^0=K^1=\begin{pmatrix}29/5&-12/5\\8/5&1/5\end{pmatrix}
\]
with ordered spectrum \((5,1)\), full conditional type effects
\[
\tau_1=(1/25,0,-1/25),\quad
\tau_2=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),
\]
and aggregate effect \(\tau=(3/400,-1/80,1/200)\).  Its at-risk masses satisfy \(\alpha_j^d=1/2\), its type contributions are
\[
\nu_1=(1/50,0,-1/50),\quad
\nu_2=(-1/80,-1/80,1/40),
\]
and its at-risk effects satisfy \(\eta_j=\tau_j\).

The laws \(P^A\) and \(P^B\) both belong to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), induce the same observed five-date law, satisfy \(P^A(X_1=e\mid D=d)=P^B(X_1=e\mid D=d)=1/5\), and have the same active-slice arrays and the same displayed cycle product.  Their full type shares are, in both cohorts,
\[
(\pi_1^{A,d},\pi_2^{A,d})=(3/5,2/5),\quad
(\pi_1^{B,d},\pi_2^{B,d})=(2/5,3/5),
\]
and their full conditional type effects are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_1^A&=(2/75,0,-2/75),&
\tau_2^A&=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),\\
\tau_1^B&=(1/25,0,-1/25),&
\tau_2^B&=(-1/60,-1/60,1/30).
\end{aligned}
\]
Nevertheless the two laws have the same at-risk masses \(\alpha_1^d=\alpha_2^d=2/5\), the same type contributions
\[
\nu_1=(2/125,0,-2/125),\quad
\nu_2=(-1/100,-1/100,1/50),
\]
the same at-risk effects
\[
\eta_1=(1/25,0,-1/25),\quad
\eta_2=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),
\]
and the same entire aggregate ATT vector \(\tau=(3/500,-1/100,1/250)\).  Together with \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\), this observational-equivalence pair proves the sharp frontier: the broad absorbing model identifies active masses, unnormalized type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate ATT, but it does not identify full type shares or full conditional type effects; adding \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\) removes exactly this allocation ambiguity.
body.justification: The witness establishes nonvacuity, checks every normalization exactly, and identifies the precise role of the initial support face for the conditional targets.
body.gap: Existing absorbing-outcome DiD results do not provide a two-type multi-state observational-equivalence calculation, and generic mixture results do not isolate the initial-absorber allocation that breaks conditional ATT recovery.
body.consumer: Applied researchers can treat baseline exit as a falsifiable support diagnostic and avoid interpreting conditional latent-type effects when baseline absorbers are present.
body.proof_tex:
Write all state vectors in the order \((a,b,e)\).  We first construct the full-data law promised by \(\texttt{def:exact-witness}\), so that consistency and the cross-world claims are checked rather than inferred from an observed factorization.  Put \(R_{j,0}=Q_j\) and \(R_{j,1}=V_j\).  For \(d,r\in\{0,1\}\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), \(s_0\in\mathcal A\), and states \(s_1,s_2,u_0,w_0,u_1,w_1\in\mathcal S\), assign joint mass
\[
\begin{aligned}
&P\{D=d,Z=j,X_0(0)=X_0(1)=s_0,
X_1(0)=X_1(1)=s_1,X_2(0)=X_2(1)=s_2,\\
&\hspace{42mm}X_3(0)=u_0,X_4(0)=w_0,
X_3(1)=u_1,X_4(1)=w_1\}\\
&\quad =\frac18 H_j[s_0,s_1]Q_j[s_1,s_2]
Q_j[s_2,u_0]Q_j[u_0,w_0]
V_j[s_2,u_1]V_j[u_1,w_1].
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{1}
\]
All other configurations receive mass zero.  Every displayed matrix in \(\texttt{def:exact-witness}\) has nonnegative entries and obeys
\[
H_j\mathbf 1_3=Q_j\mathbf 1_3=V_j\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3,
\quad H_j[e,{:}]=Q_j[e,{:}]=V_j[e,{:}]=(0,0,1).              \tag{2}
\]
Successive summation of (1), using (2), gives total mass one.  Define the observed process by \(X_t=X_t(D)\).  This gives \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), while the three shared coordinates through date \(2\) give \(\texttt{ass:no-anticipation}\).  Marginalizing from (1) the continuation belonging to the other path gives, conditional on \((D,Z)\), transition sequence \((H_j,Q_j,Q_j,Q_j)\) for \(r=0\) and \((H_j,Q_j,V_j,V_j)\) for \(r=1\).  Thus \(\texttt{ass:markov-paths}\) holds.  Equation (2) proves support on \(\mathcal G\) and \(\texttt{ass:absorbing-exit}\).  Moreover,
\[
P(D=d)=\frac12,\quad P(Z=j\mid D=d)=\frac12,                \tag{3}
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:type-overlap}\), and \(\texttt{ass:two-types}\) hold.  Taking the date-\(2\) common kernel to be \(Q_j\) and the untreated first-post kernel to be \(U_j=Q_j\) verifies \(\texttt{ass:common-date-two-transition}\) and \(\texttt{ass:common-first-post-untreated-transition}\).  No common date-\(4\) restriction is needed.  Finally, \(X_0\in\mathcal A\) almost surely and the active rows of \(H_j\) have zero exit probability, so
\[
P(X_1=e\mid D=d)=0.                                          \tag{4}
\]
In particular, the witness satisfies the additional condition \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\).

We next verify the rank and spectral requirements in the definition of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  For \(x\in\mathcal A\), define the component predecessor matrix
\[
B_x[u,j]=P(X_0=u,X_1=x,Z=j\mid D=d)=\frac14H_j[u,x].          \tag{5}
\]
It is independent of \(d\), and direct substitution gives
\[
B_a=\begin{pmatrix}3/16&1/12\\1/16&1/6\end{pmatrix},\quad
B_b=\begin{pmatrix}1/16&1/6\\3/16&1/12\end{pmatrix},
\quad \det(B_a)=\frac5{192},\quad \det(B_b)=-\frac5{192}. \tag{6}
\]
Let \(D_{xy}=\operatorname{diag}(Q_1[x,y],Q_2[x,y])\).  Let row \(j\) of \(C_y^0\) be row \(y\) of \(Q_j\), and let row \(j\) of \(C_y^1\) be row \(y\) of \(V_j\).  The Markov factorization of (1) gives, entry by entry,
\[
A_{xy}^d[u,v]=\sum_{j=1}^2B_x[u,j]Q_j[x,y]C_y^d[j,v],
\quad A_{xy}^d=B_xD_{xy}C_y^d.                              \tag{7}
\]
For the active terminal minors \(\bar C_y^d=C_y^d[:,\mathcal A]\), exact calculation yields
\[
\det(\bar C_a^0)=\frac9{50},\quad
\det(\bar C_b^0)=-\frac3{100},\quad
\det(\bar C_a^1)=\frac{31}{100},\quad
\det(\bar C_b^1)=-\frac1{20}.                               \tag{8}
\]
Since
\[
\det(\bar A_{xy}^d)=\det(B_x)Q_1[x,y]Q_2[x,y]\det(\bar C_y^d), \tag{9}
\]
equations (6)--(8) give, in the order \((aa,ab,ba,bb)\),
\[
\left(\det\bar A_{aa}^0,\det\bar A_{ab}^0,
\det\bar A_{ba}^0,\det\bar A_{bb}^0\right)
=\left(\frac9{16000},-\frac3{32000},-\frac9{32000},\frac3{12800}\right), \tag{10}
\]
and
\[
\left(\det\bar A_{aa}^1,\det\bar A_{ab}^1,
\det\bar A_{ba}^1,\det\bar A_{bb}^1\right)
=\left(\frac{31}{32000},-\frac1{6400},-\frac{31}{64000},\frac1{2560}\right). \tag{11}
\]
All eight determinants are nonzero.  Therefore every active slice is nonsingular; because there are finitely many, the minimum of their positive smallest singular values is positive.  This proves \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\).

Restricting (7) to active terminal columns and substituting into the cycle product cancels all adjacent terminal and predecessor factors:
\[
\begin{aligned}
K^d
&=B_aD_{aa}\bar C_a^d(B_bD_{ba}\bar C_a^d)^{-1}
B_bD_{bb}\bar C_b^d(B_aD_{ab}\bar C_b^d)^{-1}\\
&=B_aD_{aa}D_{ba}^{-1}D_{bb}D_{ab}^{-1}B_a^{-1}.
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{12}
\]
Every inverse and division in (12) is legitimate by (6), (8), and the strictly positive active entries of \(Q_1,Q_2\).  The middle factor is
\[
D_{aa}D_{ba}^{-1}D_{bb}D_{ab}^{-1}
=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\frac{(3/5)(1/2)}{(1/5)(3/10)},
\frac{(1/5)(3/5)}{(3/10)(2/5)}\right)
=\operatorname{diag}(5,1).                                  \tag{13}
\]
Since \(B_a=48^{-1}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}9&4\\3&8\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), equations (12)--(13) imply
\[
K^d=\frac1{60}
\begin{pmatrix}45&4\\15&8\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}8&-4\\-3&9\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}29/5&-12/5\\8/5&1/5\end{pmatrix}.          \tag{14}
\]
Its trace is \(6\) and its determinant is \(5\), hence
\[
\det(\lambda I_2-K^d)=\lambda^2-6\lambda+5=(\lambda-5)(\lambda-1),
\quad g^d=\sqrt{6^2-4\cdot5}=4>0.                          \tag{15}
\]
This proves the ordered spectrum and \(\texttt{ass:simple-cycle-spectrum}\).  Equations (2)--(4), (10)--(11), and (15), together with the preceding structural checks, establish \(\omega^\star\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).

We now calculate causal contrasts directly from the potential-path law.  The uniform active initial law is invariant under both \(H_1\) and \(H_2\).  Consequently, the type-specific date-\(2\) laws in the treated cohort are
\[
p_{2,1}^1=(1/2,1/2,0)H_1Q_1=(2/5,2/5,1/5),
\quad
p_{2,2}^1=(1/2,1/2,0)H_2Q_2=(1/4,1/2,1/4).                  \tag{16}
\]
The two paths share \(X_2\) in (1).  Conditional on \((X_2,Z,D=1)\), their date-\(3\) kernels are \(V_j\) and \(Q_j\), respectively.  The definition of \(\tau_j\) and iterated expectation therefore give
\[
\tau_j=p_{2,j}^1(V_j-Q_j).                                  \tag{17}
\]
The two exact products are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_1
&=(2/5,2/5,1/5)
\begin{pmatrix}1/10&-1/10&0\\0&1/10&-1/10\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}
=(1/25,0,-1/25),\\
\tau_2
&=(1/4,1/2,1/4)
\begin{pmatrix}0&1/10&-1/10\\-1/20&-1/10&3/20\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}
=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20).
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{18}
\]
By (3), total expectation over \(Z\) gives
\[
\tau=\frac12\tau_1+\frac12\tau_2=(3/400,-1/80,1/200).      \tag{19}
\]
Equation (4) implies \(\alpha_j^d=P(Z=j\mid D=d)=1/2\).  Since there are no initially absorbed units under \(\omega^\star\), the causal definition of the unnormalized contribution gives
\[
\nu_j=P(Z=j\mid D=1)\tau_j=\frac12\tau_j.                  \tag{20}
\]
Substitution from (18) yields
\[
\nu_1=(1/50,0,-1/50),\quad
\nu_2=(-1/80,-1/80,1/40).                                   \tag{21}
\]
Conditioning additionally on \(X_1\in\mathcal A\) changes nothing under (4), so \(\eta_j=\tau_j\).

We turn to the pair in \(\texttt{def:outside-face-pair}\).  On its added component, set \(X_t(0)=X_t(1)=e\) at every date.  For either cohort and \(C\in\{A,B\}\), marginalizing the latent label gives
\[
P^C(X_{0:4}=x_{0:4}\mid D=d)
=\frac45P_{\omega^\star}(X_{0:4}=x_{0:4}\mid D=d)
+\frac15\mathbf 1\{x_{0:4}=(e,e,e,e,e)\}.                  \tag{22}
\]
Because the cohort law is unchanged, (22) proves equality of the complete observed laws of \(P^A\) and \(P^B\), not merely equality of selected moments.

Both laws satisfy every condition defining the broad class.  Consistency and no anticipation hold separately on both mixture components.  Conditional on \((D,Z)\), at an active current state the posterior probability of the all-exit component is zero, so the next-state row is the corresponding row of the original kernel; at current state \(e\), both components move to \(e\) with probability one by (2).  Hence each marginal potential path remains first-order Markov, absorption remains valid, and the common date-\(2\) and untreated first-post kernels remain \(Q_j\).  Cohort overlap is unchanged.  Each type retains active mass \((4/5)(1/2)=2/5\), so both type shares are positive.  Finally, the all-exit component enters none of the events indexing an active slice.  Thus
\[
A_{xy}^{C,d}=\frac45A_{xy}^{\omega^\star,d},\quad
\bar A_{xy}^{C,d}=\frac45\bar A_{xy}^{\omega^\star,d},
\quad x,y\in\mathcal A.                                   \tag{23}
\]
The nonzero determinants in (10)--(11) remain nonzero, proving the slice-rank condition for both laws.  In the four-factor cycle product, the scalar multipliers cancel:
\[
(4/5)(4/5)^{-1}(4/5)(4/5)^{-1}=1.                           \tag{24}
\]
Therefore both cycle products equal (14), and both laws have the same simple ordered signature \(5>1\).  This common signature also fixes the same type labels in the two laws.  We have proved \(P^A,P^B\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  Their added component also gives
\[
P^A(X_1=e\mid D=d)=P^B(X_1=e\mid D=d)=\frac15,              \tag{25}
\]
so neither law satisfies the additional no-date-\(1\)-absorption restriction.

The active component contributes \(2/5\) to each type in each cohort.  Allocating the additional \(1/5\) to type \(1\) under \(P^A\) and to type \(2\) under \(P^B\) gives
\[
(\pi_1^{A,d},\pi_2^{A,d})=(3/5,2/5),\quad
(\pi_1^{B,d},\pi_2^{B,d})=(2/5,3/5),                        \tag{26}
\]
whereas in both laws
\[
\alpha_1^d=\alpha_2^d=\frac25.                              \tag{27}
\]
To separate the causal numerator from these full type masses, define
\[
\Delta=\operatorname{onehot}(X_3(1))-\operatorname{onehot}(X_3(0)).
\]
On \(\{D=1,X_1=e\}\), consistency gives \(X_1(1)=e\), no anticipation gives \(X_1(0)=X_1(1)=e\), and absorption applied separately to both potential paths gives \(X_3(0)=X_3(1)=e\).  Hence
\[
\Delta=0\quad\text{on }\{D=1,X_1=e\}.                      \tag{28}
\]
The added all-exit component therefore contributes zero.  The retained \(\omega^\star\) component contributes \((4/5)(1/2)\tau_j^{\omega^\star}\), so for both \(C=A,B\),
\[
\nu_j^C=E_C\{\mathbf 1(Z=j)\Delta\mid D=1\}
=\frac25\tau_j^{\omega^\star}.                             \tag{29}
\]
Using (18), equation (29) becomes
\[
\nu_1^A=\nu_1^B=(2/125,0,-2/125),\quad
\nu_2^A=\nu_2^B=(-1/100,-1/100,1/50).                       \tag{30}
\]
Because the masses in (27) are positive, division is legitimate.  Equations (28)--(29) and the definition of the at-risk effect give
\[
\eta_j^C=E_C(\Delta\mid D=1,Z=j,X_1\in\mathcal A)
=\frac{\nu_j^C}{\alpha_j^1}=\tau_j^{\omega^\star}.         \tag{31}
\]
This proves the two common at-risk vectors stated in the proposition.

For the full conditional effects, (28) and total expectation within type imply
\[
\tau_j^C=E_C(\Delta\mid D=1,Z=j)=\frac{\nu_j^C}{\pi_j^{C,1}}. \tag{32}
\]
All denominators in (32) are positive by (26).  Combining (26), (30), and (32) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_1^A&=(2/75,0,-2/75),&
\tau_2^A&=(-1/40,-1/40,1/20),\\
\tau_1^B&=(1/25,0,-1/25),&
\tau_2^B&=(-1/60,-1/60,1/30).
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{33}
\]
Thus both full type shares and both full conditional type effects differ between observationally equivalent laws.  In contrast, partitioning by the two support points of \(Z\) and applying the definition of \(\nu_j\) gives the aggregate causal identity
\[
\tau^C=E_C(\Delta\mid D=1)=\sum_{j=1}^2\nu_j^C
=(3/500,-1/100,1/250),\quad C=A,B.                          \tag{34}
\]
This proves equality of the entire aggregate vector, rather than only its exit coordinate.

Because \(P^A\) and \(P^B\) induce the same observed law but give different values in (26) and (33), no functional of the observed law can equal the full type shares or full conditional type effects throughout \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  Conversely, equations (27), (30), (31), and (34) show directly that this allocation leaves all active-side targets unchanged; \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\) proves that those targets are functions of the observed law over the whole broad compatible fiber.  Finally, under \(\texttt{ass:no-date-one-absorption}\), nonnegativity gives \(P(Z=j,X_1=e\mid D=d)=0\) for every \(j,d\), and therefore \(\pi_j^d=\alpha_j^d\); then (32) becomes \(\tau_j=\nu_j/\alpha_j^1=\eta_j\).  Hence the additional support restriction removes exactly the initial-absorber allocation ambiguity exhibited by the pair.
